cards.text: Then the LORD speaks again to Moses, Israel's leader, with a message for the Israelites. This is Mags's station, Sermons, and friend, this one RINGS. It's serious, so lean in close.
First, the LORD talks about giving children to a false god named Molech.

cards.question: What does the LORD say must happen to someone who gives one of his children to Molech?

answers.text: He must be put to death
He must pay a heavy fine

cards.question: True or false: the law about giving children to Molech covers foreigners living in Israel too.
Who does the LORD tell to stone the man who gives a child to Molech?

cards.text: And the LORD adds His own word on top of that. He will set His face against that man and cut him off from his people.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say He will cut off the man who gives his offspring to Molech?

answers.text: It defiles His sanctuary and holy name
It breaks a promise made to Moses
It brings war on the whole land

cards.text: But what if the people of the land see it happen and hide their eyes? What if nobody puts the man to death?

cards.question: If the people hide their eyes and don't put to death the man who gave his child to Molech, who does the LORD set His face against?

cards.text: Then the LORD names another way to turn from Him: going to mediums or spiritists.

cards.question: What does the LORD say He will do to whoever turns to mediums or spiritists?

answers.text: Cut him off from his people
Send him out of the camp

cards.text: Then the LORD stops listing warnings for a moment. He tells His people what He wants from them.

cards.question: Right after those warnings, what does the LORD call His people to be?
True or false: the LORD also tells His people to keep His statutes and practice them.

cards.text: Then He tells them who He is in all of this.

cards.question: As He calls Israel to keep His statutes, how does the LORD describe Himself?

cards.text: He's the LORD who sanctifies, the One who makes His people holy. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know what it's like to need Someone else to make you new.
Now the LORD names a sin that comes out of the mouth: cursing.

cards.question: If anyone curses his ___ or ___, he must be put to death.

cards.text: Next the LORD lists sexual sins, like adultery and relations with close family members or with animals. Some must be put to death, while others are cut off from their people or will be childless.
Then the LORD tells them to keep all His statutes and ordinances. And He gives a reason, about the land He's bringing them to live in.

cards.question: If Israel keeps the LORD's statutes and ordinances, what won't the land do to them?

cards.text: The land itself, friend. I got moved off my spot on the counter once, and I thought THAT was rough.
Other nations live in that land right now. The LORD says He's driving them out before Israel.

cards.question: True or false: Israel is free to follow the statutes of the nations the LORD is driving out.
Why does the LORD say He abhorred the nations He's driving out?

cards.text: Now the LORD turns back to Israel, and to what's ahead for them.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD says Israel will inherit the land of the nations He's driving out.
How does the LORD describe the land He's giving Israel as an inheritance?

cards.text: Milk and honey, friend. I live on a whole planet made for cookies, and I'm STILL a little jealous.

cards.question: The LORD reminds Israel who He is. What does He say He has done with them, compared to the other peoples?

cards.text: Being set apart reaches all the way down to the animals.

cards.question: You are therefore to distinguish between ___ and ___ animals and birds.

cards.text: Then comes that call again: be holy. This time the LORD says to be holy to Him.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say Israel is to be holy to Him?
True or false: the LORD says He set Israel apart from the nations to be His own.

cards.text: One last law closes it out, and it's about mediums and spiritists themselves.

cards.question: What does the LORD say must happen to a man or a woman who is a medium or spiritist?

answers.text: They must bring a guilt offering

cards.text: And that's where we'll set the timer for now. Friend, the LORD's teaching on being holy isn't done yet.

findings.problem: The card calls Molech "a false god." Leviticus 20:2 doesn't say who or what Molech is, and the card cites only 20:2, so this outside fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The right answer says the man "defiles His sanctuary and holy name." Leviticus 20:3 says he "defiled My sanctuary and profaned My holy name." The answer swaps "profaned" for "defiled" for the name.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card explains the hard word "sanctifies" as "the One who makes His people holy." Card words shouldn't be spent defining it, because the dictionary pop-up covers it.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The card repeats Leviticus 20:8, which cards 15 and 16 already covered, and adds a personal aside. It doesn't move the passage forward, so it works as a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The card is only a joke ("I got moved off my spot on the counter once"). It tells no part of the passage, because card 3 already covered 20:22.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card is only a joke about milk and honey. It tells no part of the passage, because card 10 already covered that detail of 20:24.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Because the land requires it" could be argued from Leviticus 20:22, which ties keeping the statutes to the land not vomiting Israel out. A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The two blanks ("father" / "mother") can be swapped. "Curses his mother or father" is just as true to Leviticus 20:9, but the answer key ties each word to one blank. Stop 2 card 14 ("clean" / "unclean") has the same issue.
findings.question: When the two right words in a two-blank card can be swapped and still match the text's meaning, should both orders count as right? Or should the writer avoid two-blank cards where the order can be swapped?
